title: Today's rivers and lakes: Natural Earth 10 m river centrelines and HydroLAKES, the present grid's own drainage and its lakes with their mean depths
note: Two archives. Natural Earth 10 m rivers and lake centrelines (version 5.0.0): 1,473 features in WGS84 longitude/latitude with a size rank (scalerank, 1 the largest rivers to 12) and a class (River, River (Intermittent), Lake Centerline, Canal); the regional supplements are not used, so every continent is drawn to the same standard. HydroLAKES v1.0: 1,427,688 lake polygons of 10 ha and more with the mean depth (Depth_avg, m, volume over area) and the surface elevation; the Caspian included. scripts/present_water.py rasterises the rivers (canals left out) as lines carrying their size, the lakes of 100 km2 or more with their mean depth (islands left dry), and the texels of the lakes the grid holds at or below its datum (the Caspian, the Dead Sea) onto the present grid's texture, cached as paleodem-0000-present-water.npz with a key of the grid, this manifest and the rules; scripts/build_rivers.py cuts the present grid's routing surface along the rivers, deeper the larger, lets the water out of the grid where a river meets the sea and in those below-datum lakes at every sea level, and paints the lakes. Only the shapefile members of HydroLAKES are extracted and its 820 MB archive is deleted afterwards; its technical documentation PDF is in the archive. HydroRIVERS was tried and dropped: its licence is the WWF HydroSHEDS agreement, not CC BY.
